title: Quasi-Hopf, Weak Hopf, and Relative Tensor Products

items.title: Quasi-bialgebras, quasi-antipodes, and quasi-Hopf algebras
items.statement: Fixes the algebraic quasi-coassociativity, reassociator pentagon and normalization, quasi-antipode equations, and the convention that quasi-Hopf requires bijective antipode.
items.strategy: Define the quasi-bialgebra data and equations in the EGNO/Haußer–Nill convention; add quasi-antipode data as a separate structure.
items.axiom_use: None; the definition is over an arbitrary field and uses only algebraic tensor products.

sources.title: P. Etingof, S. Gelaki, D. Nikshych, and V. Ostrik, Tensor Categories
F. Haußer and F. Nill, Doubles of Quasi-Quantum Groups

items.title: Weak bialgebras, weak Hopf algebras, and counital maps
items.statement: Fixes the multiplicative but possibly nonunital coproduct, weak unit/counit identities, source/target counital maps, and separate weak antipode axioms.
items.strategy: State the standard weak-bialgebra axioms and define the counital maps, then add the weak-Hopf antipode.
items.axiom_use: None; the definition uses no choice principle.

sources.title: P. Etingof, S. Gelaki, D. Nikshych, and V. Ostrik, Tensor Categories
P. Schauenburg, Weak Hopf Algebras and Quantum Groupoids

items.title: Modules over a quasi-bialgebra form a monoidal category
items.statement: For every quasi-bialgebra, the algebraic diagonal tensor action, unit k_epsilon, associator acting by Phi, and canonical unit maps make all unital left modules a monoidal category.
items.strategy: Check the diagonal action, H-linearity of the Phi associator and unit maps, then compute the pentagon and triangle as the defining identities.
items.axiom_use: None; the proof uses finite algebraic tensor sums and no choice.

sources.title: P. Etingof, S. Gelaki, D. Nikshych, and V. Ostrik, Tensor Categories
F. Haußer and F. Nill, Doubles of Quasi-Quantum Groups

items.title: Counital bases of a weak bialgebra
items.statement: Proves the source/target projections, commuting counital base algebras, their anti-isomorphism, the target separability idempotent, and the identities needed for the module tensor unit.
items.strategy: Expand the counital maps with the weak unit and weak counit equations; verify the Frobenius and counital-base identities directly.
items.axiom_use: None; all sums are the finite Sweedler expansions of algebraic tensors.

sources.title: P. Etingof, S. Gelaki, D. Nikshych, and V. Ostrik, Tensor Categories
P. Schauenburg, Weak Hopf Algebras and Quantum Groupoids

items.title: Quasi-Hopf and weak-Hopf extensions change different axioms
items.statement: Records that quasi data relax strict coassociativity while weak data relax the unit/counit axioms; the classes overlap at ordinary Hopf algebras.
items.strategy: Compare the axioms stated in the two definitions without claiming the two classes are disjoint.
items.axiom_use: Not applicable; this is a convention and scope remark.

sources.title: P. Etingof, S. Gelaki, D. Nikshych, and V. Ostrik, Tensor Categories
P. Schauenburg, Weak Hopf Algebras and Quantum Groupoids

items.title: Weak-bialgebra module tensor products are relative tensor products
items.statement: Shows V tensor over H_t W is naturally Delta(1)(V tensor_k W), with the diagonal H action, target-base unit, and associative module tensor product.
items.strategy: Use the separability idempotent to identify the balanced quotient with the Delta(1) image; check stability, associativity, unit maps, pentagon and triangle.
items.axiom_use: None; the construction is algebraic and choice-free.

title: Quasi-Hopf, Weak Hopf, and Relative Tensor Products: Examples and Counterexamples

items.title: A quasi-bialgebra need not be quasi-Hopf
items.statement: The bialgebra of a two-element idempotent monoid with Phi=1 is quasi-bialgebra but cannot admit a quasi-antipode.
items.strategy: Assume a quasi-antipode; normalize it to an ordinary antipode and contradict invertibility of the nontrivial idempotent group-like basis element.
items.axiom_use: None; the algebra and basis are explicit and finite.

sources.title: P. Etingof, S. Gelaki, D. Nikshych, and V. Ostrik, Tensor Categories

items.title: The algebra of a two-object discrete groupoid is weak Hopf
items.statement: The two-idempotent algebra with diagonal coproduct and counit 1 on each object is weak Hopf, with nonunital Delta and nonmultiplicative counit; its relative product is the diagonal subspace.
items.strategy: Verify weak bialgebra and antipode equations on the two idempotents, compute the bases and Delta(1) image, and compute the balanced quotient.
items.axiom_use: None; the algebra has two basis idempotents and the module decomposition is explicit.

sources.title: P. Etingof, S. Gelaki, D. Nikshych, and V. Ostrik, Tensor Categories
P. Schauenburg, Weak Hopf Algebras and Quantum Groupoids

items.title: A quasi-Hopf structure from a normalized 3-cocycle on C2
items.statement: The function algebra of C2 with omega(a,b,c)=(-1)^(abc) satisfies the quasi-bialgebra and quasi-antipode identities and has reassociator acting by -1 on three degree-1 modules.
items.strategy: Check the structure maps, the sixteen pentagon cases via the mod-2 exponent identity, the four quasi-antipode equations on the two idempotents, and the module associator value.
items.axiom_use: None; all structure maps and finite cases are explicit.
